keyFindings.description:
Regression: typedListBlankInItem and unclosedTypedCodeBlankInItem refuse quoted forms the browser reads tight and the merged base read alike. Measured by the reviewer: `> - a
>   C
>   - x
>
>   :::
`, `> - a
>   C
>   - x
>
`, `> - a
>   C
>       code
>
` were accepted at cc0334716bb1 and are refused at 51a234b7, and the headless engine reads every list_item spread=false. Only the closed-code quoted form (`...code
>
>   :::
`) is spread in the browser. The census rollout claim (0 newly refused that the base read correctly) is false for these.

Silent misreads of the same family remain: a blank or whitespace-only line before a typed block's closing fence in a list item spreads the item in the browser while Go reads it tight and writes the line away. Measured: `- a
  C
  para

  :::
`, `- a
  C
  > - x

  :::
`, and the architect's quote form `- a
  C
  > x
  >     code
     
  :::
` (21 tester documents) are list_item spread=true in the engine and accepted tight by ParseForWrite. Refuse the family by one named rule.

The kind 6 exemption lets `- a

  	<div x
` be stored: Go reads text `<div x` (stored `\<div x`), the browser reads html(`<div x`); every other kind 6 line it lets through fails the read-back check anyway. Exempt kind 7 only; fix comment, AGENTS.md and changelog.
Kinds compared as bare integers in four places; use goldmark's ast.HTMLBlockType constants as raw_html.go does.
The reason given for refusing kinds 1-5 wherever they stand is false for a single-line block (`> \t<!-- c -->\n` reads alike); give the true reason (goldmark refuses the same block without the tab).
quotedListIn never reads `list`, and `typed` equals `directive != nil`; blanksEndingTheList (:605) adds a three-result helper for two call sites.
typedBlankInTheItem beside sourceLines.typedBlankInItem differ only by 'The'; 'holds holds' typo.
